That puts the purchase summary under `phases[name == "purchase"].summary` (`pass_contract.py:119-131`). `scripts/cutover_234_checks.py:145` already reads it from there. `fetch_estimate` passes the whole payload to `judge_estimate`. The full run and `--estimate` both stop there, so the PM never gets the ceiling command. The test fixtures were written by hand in the inner `plan_summary` shape, which is why the tests pass anyway.

### [FAIL] F2: KEEP. A real estimate never reaches BUY
category: correctness
location: scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:242-245

`evaluate_spend(..., estimate_only=True)` always sets `VerdictStatus.ESTIMATE_ONLY` (`spend_guard.py:266-267`). `plan_summary` only writes `nothing_to_buy` when there is no spend at all (`purchase_plan.py:303`). So the estimate the full run fetches never says `"allowed"`. Once the ceiling checks pass, `judge_estimate` refuses every non-empty plan at the `!= VERDICT_ALLOWED` check. The decision needs to come from the ceilings and from `reasons`, not from the verdict string.
